newsitem.title: USA: Oregon unemployment rate rose to 5.1 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: Oregon unemployment rate rose to 5.1 pct in June.

text.p: Oregon's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate increased one-tenth of a percentage point to 5.1 percent in June, the state said on Tuesday.
Portland and Eugene reported unemployment rates below the statewide average, the Oregon Employment Department said.

"The labor markets are tight in the metropolitan areas," said David Cooke, an economist with the department. "As we move into the summer and early fall, the time of year with the most demand for workers, many employers may find it challenging to attract qualified workers for job openings."

The department said 2,300 jobs were added to the state's economy in June on a seasonally adjusted basis. Gains in construction, trade and services were only partially offset by declines in manufacturing, the department said.
Construction led June's employment growth by adding 1,800 jobs. Retail trade added 1,100 jobs in June, while services posted a seasonally adjusted job gain of 500.

Manufacturing posted a 1,600 seasonally adjusted job decline in June. Despite the drop, over the past 12 months manufacturing has been a leading sector of Oregon's economy, expanding by 10,400 jobs, or 4.4 percent.
